sentences.text:
Sri B.M.Sharad Another vs State Of Ap., on 30 June, 2022
The Honourable Sri Justice A.Santhosh Reddy
 CRL.P.No.13775 Of 2013
Order:

entities.text: B.M.Sharad Another vs State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This criminal petition is filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash the proceedings against the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 in C.C.No.299 of 2007, on the file of learned Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet by setting aside the order dated 03.07.2009 in Crl.M.P.No.3337 of 2008 passed the learned Magistrate, wherein said petition filed by the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 seeking discharge was dismissed and on revision, the learned Judge, Family Court-cum-VIII-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar by judgment dated 19.07.2013 in Crl.R.P.No.48 of 2011 confirmed the order passed by the learned Magistrate.
2. Heard both sides.
Perused the record.

3. The Food Inspector, S.S.Gutta, Mahabubnagar filed a complaint before the learned Magistrate against the petitioners herein and another for the offences punishable under Sections 16(1)(a) (1)
read with Section 2(ia)(b) and Section 7(i)of the Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, 1954 against the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 and A-1.
4.

entities.text: Prevention of Food and Adulteration Act, 1954
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The allegations in the complaint, in brief, are that on 25.08.2004, the Food Inspector visited the shop of A-1 and found about 15 kgs of Tata Agni Dust Tea packet each containing 250 gms kept in carton box along with other food items.
The Food Inspector purchased 3 packets.
Later, the Food Inspector drew samples as per the procedure prescribed and sent the same to the Public Analyst for analysis.
The Public Analyst in his report opined that the sample contains 288 ppm of iron filings which is against the prescribed stands and is thus adulterated.
Later, the Food Inspector filed complaint before the learned Magistrate against the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 and A-1 alleging offences as stated above.
5. The petitioners/A-2 and A-3 filed Crl.M.P.No.3337 of 2008 before the learned Magistrate under Section 245 Cr.P.C seeking to discharge them from the offences registered against them.
The learned Magistrate vide order dated 03.07.2009 dismissed the said petition.
Aggrieved thereby, the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 filed Crl.R.P.No.48 of 2011 before the learned Judge, Family Court- cum-VIII-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar.

entities.text: Family Court- cum-VIII-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Additional District and Sessions Judge vide judgment dated 19.07.2013 dismissed the revision petition and confirmed the order passed by the learned Magistrate.
Not satisfied with the same, the petitioners/A-2 and A-3 preferred the present criminal petition.

6. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor submits that as per the orders dated 02.11.2017 issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the Commissioners of Food Safety of all the States were directed not to launch for non-conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016 and were advised to withdraw all such prosecutions Sri B.M.Sharad Another vs State Of Ap., on 30 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80004396/
1 launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: B.M.Sharad Another vs State Of Ap
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, she submits that the prosecution of petitioners/A-2 and A-3 in the present case would not survive and prays for passing appropriate orders.

7. Keeping in view the orders dated 02.11.2017 and the letter dated 20.06.2022 addressed by the Food Safety Officer, Mahabubanagar to the learned Public Prosecutor to withdraw all prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under the FSS Act or PFA Act, the prosecution of petitioners/A-2 and A-3 does not survive and is not maintainable.
8. In view of the above, the criminal petition is allowed.

The proceedings in C.C.No.299 of 2005, on the file of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet, Mahabubnagar District and the judgment of the learned Judge, Family Court-cum-VIII- Additional District and Session Judge,
Mahabubnagar dated 19.07.2013 passed in Crl.R.P.No.48 of 2011, are hereby quashed.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Narayanpet, Mahabubnagar District
entities.label: COURT

entities.text:
Family Court-cum-VIII- Additional District and Session Judge,
Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 9. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, stand closed.

A.SANTHOSH REDDY, J 30.06.2022 Lrkm Sri B.M.Sharad Another vs State Of Ap., on 30 June, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80004396/
